title: FancyZones: Bottom of windows being snapped underneath taskbar.
author: crutkas
summary: FancyZones can cache or receive stale monitor work-area geometry after startup, wake, docking, taskbar, or DPI changes, causing zones and snapped windows to extend under the taskbar.
next_action: Approve a work-area invalidation design and reproduce dock/wake/DPI transitions.

confidence.rationale: The stale-work-area mechanism is strongly supported, but reports indicate multiple Windows and PowerToys event-order variants.

judgment.rationale: Years of reports consistently tie FancyZones using the wrong work area to startup, display wake/docking, monitor-layout, taskbar, or DPI transitions. Refreshing Windows display/work-area state often repairs it, so the remaining uncertainty is the invalidation event rather than whether the bug exists.
evidence: The issue has 84 comments and many duplicate reports across PowerToys versions.
Reopening the editor, toggling scaling, changing monitor arrangement, restarting Explorer, or reconnecting a display repairs the state for subsets of users.
The latest report reproduces on mixed 125%/100% displays connected through a Thunderbolt dock.
The FancyZones editor itself can show zones extending under the taskbar, proving stale work-area geometry before window placement.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a work-area invalidation design and reproduce dock/wake/DPI transitions.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Revalidate FancyZones work areas after shell and display transitions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: FancyZones can initialize or retain monitor work-area rectangles before the taskbar/display topology has settled, and it does not reliably rebuild them after every relevant shell, DPI, wake, or docking transition.
plan: Centralize monitor/work-area refresh for startup, WM_SETTINGCHANGE work-area events, display/DPI changes, power resume, and topology changes.
Debounce transition bursts and compare the work-area rectangle with the current monitor/taskbar geometry before applying layouts.
Recalculate active layouts and window placements only after stable geometry is observed, with telemetry/logging for rejected stale values.
verification: Exercise boot, monitor sleep/wake, Thunderbolt dock attach/detach, KVM switching, taskbar auto-hide, and mixed-DPI changes.
Verify the editor and snapped windows stay inside each monitor's current work area and recover without restarting Explorer or toggling scaling.

confidence.rationale: The stale-work-area mechanism is strongly supported, but reports indicate multiple Windows and PowerToys event-order variants.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones can cache or receive stale monitor work-area geometry after startup, wake, docking, taskbar, or DPI changes, causing zones and snapped windows to extend under the taskbar.
known_information: The bug spans single and multi-monitor systems and many PowerToys releases.
It often begins after boot, display sleep/wake, docking/KVM changes, or display reconfiguration.
Different refresh operations repair the issue for different users.
Some users also observe incorrect Windows Snap geometry, while others reproduce only with FancyZones.
inferences: FancyZones is not consistently invalidating and rebuilding work-area data when shell/display topology becomes stable.
There may be multiple upstream triggers, so the fix should validate geometry rather than rely on one event ordering.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is already highly reproducible in aggregate. A safe PowerToys fix can subscribe to relevant work-area/display changes, debounce unstable transitions, and reject obviously inconsistent work-area rectangles before applying layouts.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete 84-comment live discussion, current labels, assignment, and the consolidated duplicate timeline.
Separated reports that also affect Windows Snap from reports where FancyZones-specific refresh operations change the outcome.

actions.label: Reproduce stale work-area geometry
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact does not execute the steps or write upstream.

reproduce.version_requirement: Latest stable or Preview PowerToys build
prerequisites: At least two displays with mixed scaling or a dock/KVM
FancyZones enabled with a layout touching the work-area bottom
steps: Confirm zones initially stop above the taskbar.
Sleep/wake displays or attach/detach the dock/KVM.
Open the layout editor and inspect the zone boundary before changing settings.
Toggle display scaling or monitor arrangement and note whether geometry repairs.
reproduce.expected_result: The exact transition that leaves stale work-area bounds is captured, and a subsequent refresh keeps zones above the taskbar.
